newsitem.title: UK: UK oil, gas output to reach 5 mln boe in 1999 - report.
newsitem.headline: UK oil, gas output to reach 5 mln boe in 1999 - report.

text.p: British Continental Shelf oil and gas production is forecast to exceed an average of five million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) per day in 1999, consultants Arthur Andersen said on Monday.
This production would comprise a record 3.24 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil and liquids and 10.3 billion standard cubic feet per day of gas, an Arthur Andersen statement said.
The statement was based on research by Arthur Andersen Petroleum Services Group to be published in the company's 1997 UK Continental Shelf Summary Book.
The January 1996 edition forecast 1999 production to peak at 4.6 million boe per day.

The statement added that the 8.7 percent increase in the forecast was attributable mainly to oil production because operations were influenced by a rise in the oil price during 1996, with Brent blend averaging over $20 a barrel in that year, the statement said.

The 1997 edition forecasts oil and gas production at 4.462 million boe per day in 1997, 4.756 million boe per day in 1998 and 5.009 million boe per day in 1999, falling to 4.947 million boe per day in 2000.

The statement said the increase in production could also be explained partly by the rise in recoverable oil reserves to 27.3 billion barrels forecast in the 1997 edition from 26.5 billion barrels forecast in the 1996 edition.
